description: Pozytywne świry z informatyki stosowanej UJ
summary:
MIRROR-MED is an autonomous health monitoring station that costs astronauts zero crew time. During the daily planning briefing the crew attends anyway, a camera reads the face and extracts dozens of health signals: heart rate and HRV (remote photoplethysmography), breathing, blinks and eyelid closure, gaze, facial asymmetry and puffiness, expression and tension. Each value is compared with the astronaut's own baseline rather than a population average, and the system looks for patterns instead of single numbers to avoid false alarms.

It produces two reports. The astronaut gets a plain-language summary with concrete actions. The Medical Officer gets a full console: crew board sorted by urgency, findings linked to NASA Human Research Program risks, 30-day trends, follow-up orders, and a live view of eight imaging layers. Multi-day analysis flags accumulating fatigue and early low-mood signs as screening, never as diagnosis. Escalation advice adapts to communication delay (ISS, Moon, Mars). A laptop only has an RGB camera, so thermal, NIR, UV, hyperspectral, depth and pupillometry layers are simulated and labelled as such everywhere.
